The '''2010–11 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Colorado]] in the [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Head coach [[Tad Boyle]] was in his first season at Colorado. The Buffaloes competed in the [[2010–11 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12 Conference]] and played their home games at the [[Coors Events Center]].

This was the Buffaloes' last season in the Big 12, as they moved to the [[Pac-12 Conference]] in 2011,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?&ATCLID=204998596&DB_OEM_ID=10410 |title=Terms for Colorado Withdrawal From Big 12 Announced |work=[[Big 12 Conference]] |accessdate=September 21, 2010}}</ref> before returning to the Big 12 in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-27 |title=CU later: Board approves Buffs' return to Big 12 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/38083687/colorado-board-unanimously-approves-move-pac-12-big-12 |access-date=2024-11-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Preseason==
The Buffaloes finished the previous season with a record of 15–16 and 6–10 in Big 12 Conference play. Of those 16 losses, seven were by six points or less. Additionally, all five starters return from that team.<ref name=king/>

In the Big 12 preseason coaches' poll, the Buffaloes were picked to finish ninth. [[Cory Higgins]] was named the Preseason All-Conference First Team, while [[Alec Burks]] was an honorable mention.<ref name=longmont>
{{cite news|first=Brian|last=Howell|url=http://www.timescall.com/sports_story.asp?id=23873|title=CU sets out to exceed expectations|accessdate=January 11, 2011|date=October 16, 2010|work=[[Longmont Times-Call]]}}{{Dead link|date=April 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}
</ref> Both were also named to the 50-man preseason [[Wooden Award]] watchlist.<ref name=wooden>{{cite web|url=http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=861|title=2010–2011 Men's Preseason Top 50 List|work=[[John R. Wooden Award]]|accessdate=November 12, 2010| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20101010122040/http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=861| archivedate= October 10, 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> Additionally, Burks was on the 50-man preseason [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] watchlist.<ref name=naismith>{{cite web|url=http://www.shupirates.com//pdf8/723283.pdf|title=Duke University Leads a Diverse Pack on the Naismith Preseason Watchlist|work=MSL Atlanta|accessdate=November 16, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120310171045/http://www.shupirates.com//pdf8/723283.pdf|archive-date=March 10, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Gary Parrish]] picked them eighth in the Big 12, and said that he "won't be shocked if they ride the Higgins-Burks tandem into the top half of the league and make the NCAA tournament for the first time since 2003."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/14241463/big-12-preview-competition-could-breed-national-contender|title=Big 12 preview: Competition could breed national contender|first=Gary|last=Parrish|work=[[CBS Sports]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=November 4, 2010|accessdate=January 12, 2011| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20101229214156/http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/14241463/big-12-preview-competition-could-breed-national-contender| archivedate= December 29, 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> Jason King of [[Rivals.com]] named the Buffaloes the sixth-best team in conference, adding, "Don't be surprised if long-suffering Colorado sneaks into the NCAA tournament."<ref name=king>{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketball.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=1145850|title=League preview: Big 12|first=Jason|last=King|work=[[Rivals.com]]|publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|date=October 31, 2010|accessdate=January 12, 2011}}</ref>

==Season==

===Preconference season===
The Buffaloes defeated in-state rivals [[Colorado State]] 93–80 in overtime, behind [[Alec Burks]]' 25 points. Marcus Relphorde contributed 18 points and Cory Higgins added 15. Levi Knutson hit four free throws in the final 57 seconds to seal the victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=303420038|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110228111042/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=303420038|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 28, 2011|title=Colorado 90, Colorado St. 83|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=December 8, 2010|accessdate=January 12, 2011}}</ref>

===Big 12 season===
Snapping a losing streak of 13 consecutive conference openers, Colorado knocked off No. 8 [[2010–11 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]] 89–76 as [[Alec Burks]] exploded for a career-high 36 points. This was the Buffaloes' first win over a top ten team since defeating No. 3 [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] in 2003. [[Cory Higgins]] had 18 points and a career-tying 10 rebounds. The Buffaloes had a 12-point halftime lead and never let Missouri get closer than seven in the second half.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310080038|title=Colorado star Alec Burks scores 36, helps hand No. 8 Missouri a second loss|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=January 8, 2011|access-date=January 14, 2011| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110227075010/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310080038| archive-date= February 27, 2011 | url-status= dead}}</ref>

===Post-season===
The Buffs were selected as the No. 1 seed for the 2011 NIT Tournament.
